baselineScopeTemplate: Does retained evidence ${source.id} address the same referent, factual relation and material time, place and population circumstances as the proposition without guessing? Assess scope separately from agreement: a different asserted value, location or date can directly refute the claim and is not itself a scope mismatch. For example, evidence naming a different capital of the same country addresses the same relation; evidence about another country, period or population does not. An in-scope counterexample can refute a universal claim; a limited sample cannot substantiate a universal claim about all places, times or people.
baselineStanceTemplate: For retained evidence ${source.id}, judge its stance on the checked proposition itself, not whether someone said it. A citation title or authority alone proves nothing.
priorScope16Replacement: Does this retained passage address the same identified subject and factual relation, with the same material restrictions that determine which event, observation or population the proposition concerns? Separate the value being tested from restrictions on the comparison. A different asserted value of the same relation—including an event date, place, name, category, count or quantity—can directly contradict the claim and is not itself a scope mismatch. A different observation period, population, jurisdiction, version, episode or materially qualified relation is a mismatch even when the subject and topic overlap. Preserve qualifiers such as first, latest, original, revised, all and only, plus any condition: a repeated event does not establish the first event unless the passage explicitly relates them. An in-scope counterexample may refute a universal claim, while a limited sample cannot support the universal. Use only the retained passage and exact proposition; do not complete missing referents or restrictions from world knowledge, a title or source prestige. Scope is separate from stance, substantive basis and reliability. If matching the material restrictions requires guessing, answer no.
